prompt: What is the sum, in degrees, of the interior angles of a pentagon?
hint: Any polygon can be cut into triangles from one corner. The number of triangles depends on the number of sides.

hints.text: Any polygon can be cut into triangles from one corner. The number of triangles depends on the number of sides.
An $n$-sided polygon has an angle sum of $(n - 2) \times 180°$. A pentagon has $5$ sides, so work out $(5 - 2) \times 180$.
Since $3 \times 180 = 540$, the interior angles of a pentagon add up to $540$ degrees.

explanation: A polygon with $n$ sides can be divided into $n - 2$ triangles, and each triangle contributes $180°$.
A pentagon has $5$ sides, so it divides into $5 - 2 = 3$ triangles.
The angle sum is $3 \times 180 = 540$, so the interior angles total $540$ degrees.

alternativeExplanations.title: Derive it rather than memorize it
steps: Pick one vertex and draw diagonals to every non-adjacent vertex.
A pentagon splits into exactly $3$ triangles this way, which is where the $n - 2$ comes from.
If you blank on the formula, drawing the triangles rebuilds it in ten seconds.
